topic: Same $100,000 profit, Manitoba 2026: sole proprietor vs a CCPC paying all profit as non-eligible dividends vs a CCPC leaving $40,000 inside

example.note: example (not a CRA rule): single Manitoba resident, no other income, $100,000 net business profit in 2026; corporation is a CCPC eligible for the small business deduction (9% federal + 0% Manitoba), all after-tax profit paid as non-eligible dividends in the same year; costs of the corporation (incorporation, accounting, T2) not included. Computed by c1/calc.py.

sources.gross_up: ITA 82(1)(b)(i): non-eligible dividends grossed up by 15% (taxation years after 2018); laws.justice.gc.ca, current to 2026-09-30
sources.fed_dtc: ITA 121(a)(ii): federal dividend tax credit 9/13 of the gross-up (after 2018); same
sources.mb_dtc: Manitoba Income Tax Act C.C.S.M. c. I10 s.4.7(1)(b)(i.2): 0.7835% of the grossed-up amount for dividends with a federal gross-up of 17% or lower; web2.gov.mb.ca, current from 2026-07-01, accessed 2026-10-16
sources.corp_rates: CRA 'Corporation tax rates' and Manitoba small business rate 0% on the first $500,000 (as recorded and sourced in c3/PRODUCTION-BIBLE.md, R1)
sources.cpp: CPP 2026: YMPE $74,600, YAMPE $85,000, basic exemption $3,500; self-employed pay both halves (11.9% + 8% CPP2); CPP Act ss.12–13: contributions only on salary/wages and self-employed earnings (dividends are neither)
sources.rrsp: ITA 146(1) 'earned income': employment, business carried on, rental/royalty income; dividends are not included
sources.personal_rates: CRA T4127 (2026) federal brackets/BPA $16,452; Manitoba brackets 10.8/12.75/17.4% and BPA $15,780 (2026, frozen)
sources.cross_check: Manitoba non-eligible top combined rate implied by these credits = 46.67%, matching KPMG and EY 2026 tables
